_note: v3 (zero-shot, text only): one change vs v2: each prompt also carries a short visual symptom description of the disease (knowledge/disease_descriptions_v1.json: colour, lesion shape, margins, rings/halos, signs such as powder or pustules). v1/v2 showed CLIP knows crops but not diseases (disease correct ~10%); the disease NAME often means nothing to CLIP (sigatoka, esca), but the visual words in the description do. This is the knowledge-guided part of the proposed approach, tested here without training. Caveat: the descriptions were written by Claude from general plant-pathology knowledge and are unverified.
_result: Large gain from the descriptions alone: harmonic mean 10.2% (v2 5.6%), top-5 HM 30.0% (v2 22.2%); seen top-1 7.8% / top-5 26.4%, unseen top-1 14.6% / top-5 34.8%. Disease correct 15% seen / 17% unseen (v2 10.5% / 8%). The unseen gain is uneven: grape_black_rot 8% -> 59% (its description, tan spots with dark borders and black dots, matches the images), cucumber_downy_mildew 0 -> 22%, sugarcane_rust 0 -> 10%, cherry_aphis_spp 0 -> 8%; but tomato_early_blight (1/3 of test_unseen) stays near 0 (0.6%) and pepper_bell_bacterial_spot at 3%, both pulled to coffee_cercospora, which remains a hub prompt. Zero-shot ceiling so far: the text helps, but without training the scores are badly calibrated across classes.

names._note: Unchanged from v2 (same overrides; segatoka kept because banana_segatoka and banana_sigatoka are separate classes).

prompts._note: Same five templates as v2 with ': {description}' appended, so the only difference from v2 is the description. Healthy classes get the description 'uniformly green leaves with no spots...'. zeroshot.py fails if any prompt exceeds CLIP's 77 tokens.
templates: a close-up photo of a {crop} leaf showing {disease}: {description}.
a field photo of {crop} leaves with {disease}: {description}.
healthy_templates: a close-up photo of a healthy {crop} leaf: {description}.
a field photo of healthy {crop} leaves: {description}.
